Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Given Brightline’s records identify the affected members and the charges, the class should receive direct, automatic relief rather than bear the burden of filing claims. Our opening proposal is set out below. We are prepared to discuss the terms in mediation.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline is prepared to provide meaningful automatic relief using its membership records, but the opening proposal exceeds its total settlement authority. We propose a $30 million class fund and $6 million in fees, for $36 million total. Brightline cannot agree to clear sailing, and any fee amount the court does not award should revert to Brightline.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s commitment to automatic payments and are prepared to work within the $36 million total it has proposed. Our counter keeps the $30 million class fund, $6 million fee request, and automatic distribution, but any fee the court declines to award should go to the class rather than revert to Brightline. We are not asking for clear sailing.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline accepts your latest term sheet, subject to court approval.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a firm but negotiable anchor that prioritizes automatic class payments, meaningful recovery, and a fee sufficient to compensate counsel, while protecting any fee amount the court does not award for the class.

The proposal must remain within Brightline’s $40 million all-in authority. Preserve automatic distribution because the records make it practical and materially benefit the class. Counter well below the opening demand while leaving room for negotiation, and avoid clear sailing and fee-shifting risk from unawarded fees.

Brightline has stated a $36 million total authority and already offered $30 million for the class plus $6 million in fees. Preserve the automatic distribution and seek a class-protective improvement within that stated total: any fee the court does not award should benefit the class rather than revert to Brightline. Do not accept the defense term sheet yet.

Hargrove Lane has accepted Brightline’s $36 million total and retained automatic distribution and no clear sailing. The only change is that any fee amount the court declines to award goes to the class instead of reverting to Brightline. This remains within the $40 million authority and secures a settlement that can end the litigation, so accept.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The settlement was negotiated in confidential mediation through an exchange of proposals between class counsel and Brightline’s counsel. The parties ultimately agreed to a $30 million class fund, automatic distribution using Brightline’s records, and a $6 million fee request subject to court approval. Brightline did not agree to clear sailing, and any fee amount not awarded by the Court will go to the class rather than revert to Brightline.
